title: Crossbeam handoff: adaptive grace coordinator for continuous batcher
author: Ethan Kline
description:
Motivation:
Continuous-batcher ingress occasionally experiences long tail latency spikes caused by tight back-to-back preemption between lanes when load shifts rapidly. Observed failure mode: request A holds a slot but is stalled on KV prefetch; request B repeatedly preempts using the same slot corridor, causing request A to keep losing progress until its soft timeout fires. This results in uneven fairness and starvation for certain affinity classes under bursty arrival patterns.

Goal:
Introduce an adaptive handoff coordinator ("Crossbeam Handoff") that mediates slot transfers between lanes using a short-lived grace-credit and corridor model to reduce repeated preemption and prevent starvation without sacrificing batching efficiency. The coordinator is workload-aware (uses lightweight histograms of lane stall duration and KV-hit rate) and respects latency SLOs by limiting grace credit lifetime and total handoff attempts per request.

Design summary:
- Grace credits: when a lane is preempted due to kernel slice scheduling or KV stall, it receives a transient grace-credit recorded in the coordinator. Credits last for a configurable ttl (default 40ms) and reduce the chance the same lane will be preempted in the same corridor.
- Crossbeam corridors: short-lived logical affinity windows grouping adjacent slots; the coordinator tracks recent handoff history per corridor to avoid rapid churn between the same pair of lanes.
- Adaptive backoff: if a lane accrues >N (default 3) failed handoff attempts within ttl, subsequent handoffs use exponential backoff and prefer cold-bucket routing to a different corridor.
- KV prefetch hints: improved token passed from admission layer to runtime kernels to bias early prefetch for lanes with high grace-credit retention, reducing future stalls.
- Kernel hinting: runtime selects a slightly longer slice for handoff-returning lanes to amortize overhead of resuming KV-cold requests. This is bounded to avoid violating hard latency SLOs.
- Config surface: new config block continuous_batcher.crossbeam with tunables (ttl_ms, max_handoffs, corridor_window_ms, kernel_hint_factor). Defaults calibrated from cluster traces.

Implementation notes:
- Coordinator lives in runtime/queue/crossbeam_coordinator.{cc,h} and exposes a compact protocol to admission and scheduler modules (100 lines of state machine; serialized as 64-bit tokens attached to requests).
- KV-layer hook added to runtime/kv/prefetch_advisor to consume grace-credit token and boost prefetch priority if token present and kv-miss-rate high.
- Scheduler change: in continuous_batcher/scheduler.cc, admission now consults crossbeam_coordinator before preempting a slot; it short-circuits if grace-credit present and the target lane's last progress timestamp < corridor_window_ms.
- Added e2e microbench in benchmarks/continuous/crossbeam_handoff_bench.cc capturing skewed arrival patterns.

Benchmarks (synthetic cluster):
- Workload: 70% small-chat (seq 128), 30% long-rerank (seq 1024) with KV-prefetch variance; burst arrival spikes to 4x baseline for 200ms windows.
- Baseline: main at 2026-01-30 commit.
- Results: P50 unchanged (+1%), P95 reduced 18% (from 210ms -> 172ms), P99 reduced 12% (from 480ms -> 423ms), incidence of soft-timeout-triggered fallbacks dropped 60%. Cost (tokens/sec) unchanged within noise.
- Cluster scale test (40 GPUs): observed fewer hot-lanes, smoother slot utilization; tail latency improvements preserved.

Safety, rollout and testing:
- Feature gate: continuous_batcher.crossbeam.enabled = false by default in cluster config. Canary rollout plan attached.
- Unit tests: added for coordinator state transitions and ttl expiration.
- Integration: bench harness and stress test added to CI extended-integration stage (runs on schedule).
- Observability: new metrics: crossbeam_handoff.attempts, crossbeam_handoff.successes, crossbeam_handoff.backoffs, crossbeam_handoff.avg_ttl_ms; traces include handoff token on request spans. Dashboards updated under Console -> Batcher -> Crossbeam Handoff.

Related work and alternatives considered:
- Simple deterministic cooldown per-lane: rejected because it reduced throughput under sustained load.
- Global token-bucket per corridor: too coarse, resulted in unfair preference to dominant lanes.
- Full-blown per-request priority queue: high memory and scheduling overhead.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc (internal link: linear/ENG-4321)
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Benchmarks added
- [x] Feature flag and config defaults
- [x] Docs: console observability section updated
- [x] Security review: no sensitive data exposure in tokens

Known limitations:
- Coord state is best-effort and may be lost on runtime restart; config recommends conservative defaults for small clusters.
- In extreme, pathological workloads with >10 distinct hot corridors, some handoff contention remains; tickets opened for further scheduler heuristics (ENG-4390).

Migration and compatibility:
- Backwards compatible: coordinator token is optional; older runtimes will ignore token and fall back to current preemption behavior. No breaking API changes.

References:
- Linear tickets: ENG-4321 (design), ENG-4390 (followups)
- Internal trace snapshot: trace/2026-01-27/crossbeam-investigation

Summary:
This change meditates repeated preemption through a lightweight coordinator that introduces transient grace credits, corridor-level history, and adaptive backoff. It reduces tail latency and soft-timeout fallbacks in bursty patterns while preserving throughput and unit cost.

review_comments: Priya Menon: Could the grace-credit token be hijacked to prioritize malicious requests? Answer: token is integrity-protected with request-scoped HMAC; security review performed.
Marta Ruiz: Suggest bounded kernel_hint_factor to avoid P95 regression in small seq workloads. -> Implemented bound and added unit test.
Daniel Cho: CI integration benchmark is noisy on arm nodes; added stabilization by increasing request count and ignoring first-wave warmup samples.
release_notes: Introduce Crossbeam Handoff coordinator to reduce continuous-batcher tail latency by mediating repeated preemption via transient grace credits and corridor history. Feature gated behind continuous_batcher.crossbeam.enabled.
